title: Effect of the surface on the energy levels in PbS and PbSe nanocrystals
authors: O. Lundgren, A. V. Rodina, Al. L. Efros
abstract: The structure of the electron and hole quantum confinement levels in spherical PbS and PbSe nanocrystals (NCs) is studied within the framework of a four-band effective-mass model. This level structure was initially calculated within the Kang--Wise model, which employs the standard boundary condition of vanishing carrier wave functions at the NC surface. This model, however, does not allow one to account for the effect of the NC surface on the level structure. Here, the effect of the NC surface is modeled using general boundary conditions (GBCs) imposed on the envelope wave functions at the surface. We show that the surface properties modify the size dependence of the electron and hole confinement levels and lead to an additional spin--orbit splitting of the $1P_{h,e}$ levels. Using the GBCs, we are able to quantitatively describe the size dependence of the lowest optical transitions in bare PbS and PbSe NCs and explain the differences between the absorption spectra of bare and Cl-passivated PbS NCs
summary: This paper theoretically investigates how the physical surface of PbS and PbSe nanocrystals alters their electronic energy levels. By moving beyond standard boundary conditions to use General Boundary Conditions derived from current continuity, the authors show that surface effects modify size dependence and induce spin-orbit splitting. This provides a quantitative framework to explain the differences observed between bare and chemically passivated nanocrystals.
main_problem: The study focuses on accurately modeling the quantum confinement energy levels in PbS and PbSe nanocrystals, specifically addressing how the physical surface modifies these electronic structures.
main_result: The use of General Boundary Conditions (GBCs) successfully modifies the predicted size dependence of confinement levels and predicts an additional spin-orbit splitting, allowing for quantitative comparison between bare and passivated NCs.
method: The authors employ a four-band effective-mass model and derive GBCs by enforcing the continuity of the normal component of the current density at the nanocrystal surface.
model_or_system: The system is spherical PbS and PbSe nanocrystals modeled using a four-band effective-mass Hamiltonian. The core theoretical advancement is replacing standard boundary conditions with GBCs derived from current continuity.
key_observables: Electron and hole quantum confinement levels, size dependence of optical transitions, and spin-orbit splitting of $1P_{h,e}$ levels.
important_parameters: The surface-induced parameters derived from GBCs, such as $\gamma_c, \gamma_v$, and the comparison between bare and Cl-passivated states.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes an abrupt spherical surface modeled as an impenetrable barrier, and the GBCs are derived from current density continuity.
figures_summary: Figure 6 illustrates the global fit of transition energy versus core diameter for PbS NCs, demonstrating the success of the GBC model.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by introducing the four-band model, deriving the necessary General Boundary Conditions (GBCs) from current continuity, analyzing how these GBCs modify the size dependence, and finally applying them to quantitatively describe optical transitions in bare and passivated NCs.
why_interesting: The rigorous derivation and application of GBCs to account for surface effects in semiconductor quantum dots is highly relevant to open quantum systems and quantum optics, as surface passivation and interface physics are critical for controlling exciton lifetimes and emission properties.
